I reviewed the uncommitted changes in `lib/` and reported three findings, all plausible but not confirmed. I only read the diff and `shouldBypassProxy.js`. I didn't run the tests or read the modified test files.

1. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:132`:** The check that threw on CR/LF in header values is gone. Invalid characters are now stripped silently, including any character above 0xFF. For example, `a\r\nInjected: 1` becomes `aInjected: 1` instead of throwing. A non-Latin1 value such as a CJK string loses characters with no error. Any test that expects the old throw will probably fail.
2. **`lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js:50`:** `normalizeValue` now trims leading and trailing spaces and tabs from every header value. The old code only stripped trailing CR/LF, so `'  value '` now becomes `'value'`.
3. **`lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:108`:** Any loopback entry in `NO_PROXY` now matches every loopback host. `NO_PROXY=localhost` bypasses the proxy for `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` too, and the reverse also holds. This can send traffic directly that an operator meant to proxy.

findings.summary: The CR/LF validation that threw on invalid header values was removed. Invalid characters are now silently stripped, and characters above 0xFF are dropped too.
findings.failure_scenario: Before, headers.set('X', 'a\r\nInjected: 1') threw 'Invalid character in header content'. Now it quietly becomes 'aInjected: 1' and the request goes out with a changed value. A non-Latin1 value such as 'héllo✓' or a CJK string loses the characters above 0xFF with no error. Callers who relied on the throw to reject untrusted input now get corrupted values and no signal. Existing tests that expect the throw will also fail.

findings.summary: normalizeValue now trims leading and trailing spaces and tabs from every header value. The old code only stripped trailing CR/LF.
findings.failure_scenario: headers.set('X-Pad', '  value ') now stores 'value'. Header values that depend on leading or trailing whitespace change, and Authorization or custom signed headers can stop matching what the caller computed.

findings.summary: The loopback aliasing makes any loopback NO_PROXY entry match every loopback host. This goes beyond the exact hostname match NO_PROXY normally uses.
findings.failure_scenario: With NO_PROXY=localhost, requests to http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1] now bypass the proxy. The reverse also holds: NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1 now bypasses the proxy for localhost and ::1. This is surprising, and it can send traffic directly that an operator meant to proxy, such as a proxy-based sandbox. Only exact entries should match, as in curl and Node.
